newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's DSE leaders resign over scandal.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's DSE leaders resign over scandal.

text.p: Five of nine elected members of the governing council of Bangladesh's main Dhaka Stocks Exchange (DSE) have resigned, demanding an immediate dissolution of the council and reforms, bourse officials said on Tuesday.
The officials also wanted an early election of a new body.
But DSE chairman and head of the council, Imtiyaz Husain, refused to step down, although he wanted an election to be held in June, six months ahead of schedule, the officials said.

The resignations and call for a new council poll were prompted by a recent scandal in the securities market. An official inquiry accused dozens of top dealers and company executives of manipulating share prices.
The DSE all-share index surged above 3,600 points in October-November last year before taking a sharp downturn, trading at 1,102.37 points on Monday.

Last month, an inquiry committee appointed by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), watchdog of the country's securities market, said 36 top dealers and owners of listed companies had been involved in "fraudulant activities" which created excess price volatility and led to huge losses for investors.
The accused included Husain, who has described the inquiry report as baseless and motivated.
The DSE council members who resigned on Monday were vice-chairman Ahmed Iqbal Hasan and members Khurshid Alam, Rakibur Rahman and M.G. Azam Chowdhury.
Earlier, another council member, Shamsul Alam, submitted his resignation and it was accepted, DSE officials said on Tuesday,
Husain confirmed that he received the resignation letters and said they would be accepted by the council in a few days.
The council, the highest decision-making body of the bourse, met on Monday to discuss the situation in the market, DSE sources told Reuters.
One source said the resignations were part of a move within the DSE to drive Husain from the top council position. Those who have resigned have demanded Husain step down as well.
"It's not entirely their own decision. They were rather compelled to become party to a move," one source said.
Khurshid Alam said: "I tendered my resignation at the request of the general members of the DSE. A new body will inject confidence among the investors."
"We resigned to pave the way for the reorganisation of the DSE to launch reforms immediately and hold the election as soon as possible."
Besides the nine elected members, the DSE council also has three government-nominated members.
They are the chief of Federation of Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and Industries, President of Institute of the Charterd Accountants and a Joint-Secretary of the Ministry of Finance.
Husain told Reuters on Tuesday: "I shall not resign. I was democratically elected and will not bow to any pressure."
The two-year tenure of the DSE council is due to expire in December.
